Office of the Secretary of Defense

(3) Final acceptance for the visit will be subject to the concurrence of the contractor. The contractor will notify the USG agency when a classified visit is not desired.

(B) Request visits denials. If the USG agency does not approve the request or the information related to the proposed classified visit, it will deny the classified visit request. The USG agency will advise the requesting government and the contractor to be notified of the reason for the denial.

(C) Non-sponsorship. The USG agency will decide on a request to support a USG program. If the USG agency will furnish a declination notice indicating that the classified visit is not USG-approved (i.e., the visitor is non-sponsored) to the requesting foreign government with information to the USG contractor, the contractor will be notified.

(D) A declination notice does not preclude the classified visit, provided the contractor has, or obtains, an export authorization for the information involved, and has notified the requesting foreign government has provided the required security assessment of the proposed visitor to the USG agency in the original classified visit request.

(E) Long-term classified visits and assignments of foreign nationals. Extended classified visits and assignments of foreign nationals to contractor locations can be authorized only when it is essential pursuant to a contract or government agreement (e.g., joint venture, liaison representative to a joint or multinational program, and direct commercial sale).

(1) Consult with its empowered official for guidance.

(2) Notify the CSA in advance of all long-term classified visits and assignments of foreign nationals.

(3) Provide the CSA with a copy of the approved classified visit authorization or the USG export authorization.

(4) Control of foreign visitors to U.S. contractors. (1) Contractor. The contractor will:

(A) Establish procedures to ensure that foreign visitors are not afforded access to classified information except as authorized by an export license, an approved visit request, or other exemption to the licensing requirements.

(B) Notify the foreign visitor of the scope of access authorized or of the restrictions imposed by the government.

(C) Foreign visitors. Foreign visitors will be given custody of classified material except when they are acting as official couriers of the government. The CSA authorizes the transfer.

(D) Temporary access of foreign government material at a U.S. contractor location is to remain under U.S. contractor custody and control and is subject to self-inspection and CSA security reviews.

(E) This does not preclude the contractor from furnishing a foreign visitor with a security container for the temporary storage of classified material, consistent with the purpose of the assignment, provided the CSA approves and responsibility for the container and its contents remains with the U.S. contractor.

(1) The CSA may approve exceptions to this policy on a case-by-case basis for the temporary storage of foreign government classified information furnished to the visitor by the visitor's government through government channels.
